overall: The tables support the four main estimates (H1 0.638, H2 -5.311, H3 0.166, H4 0.267) and the null-ish subgroup interaction. The wording sometimes overreaches: 'recall' mislabels keyword use in the conversation, and the E2 row is described as a within-group effect when it is an interaction coefficient. The most important caveat is that the plan is reconstructed post hoc, so every test is exploratory and uncorrected for multiple comparisons. The placebo arm also includes a chatbot, so the estimates do not isolate the chatbot's contribution.

issues.issue: Text says the hypothesis 'allowed a change in either direction', but the table labels H4 as two_sided while the hypothesis statement is 'changes'. This is a minor framing. More importantly, the Key findings say 'Recall of op-ed keywords was higher', but the H3 and H4 outcomes are keyword use in conversation, not recall of the op-ed.
issues.fix: Describe the outcomes as use of op-ed keywords in the conversation, not recall of op-ed keywords.
issues.disposition_reason: Relabel keyword outcomes as use in conversation rather than recall; numbers are unaffected.

issues.issue: The text calls 0.227 'the H3 treatment effect ... in the reported group row', yet the table term is the interaction term treat:C(_mod)[T.pro], not a group-specific slope. The text also says no interaction test was run.
issues.fix: State that 0.227 is the treat x pro interaction coefficient (n = 446), not a within-group treatment effect.
issues.disposition_reason: The 0.227 is an interaction coefficient, so the text and label need correcting.

issues.issue: The text rounds the H3 control mean to 0.09 (table 0.088), and the H1 text says p < 0.001 where the table gives 4.28e-06. These are acceptable roundings, but H2 p = 0.004 is shown as 0.000 for the intercept.
issues.fix: No substantive change; optionally report exact p-values.
issues.disposition_reason: Only rounding and p-value display; no estimate changes.
